## In two minutes

The repository combines a sample catalog/orders application with a separate GitHub Actions workflow system for producing and maintaining codebase analyses; the modules share a repository but are not one deployed service (`README.md:1-7`; [`system context`](hld/01-system-context.md)). The catalog keeps product records in process memory, provides price and stock lookups, and includes an optional HTTP server (`components/catalog/catalog.py:8-29`; `components/catalog/service.py:15-49`). The current order helpers import the catalog directly, while the HTTP price client is intended for a separately deployed orders service and is called only by tests in this repository (`components/orders/orders.py:5,19-20,35-42`; `components/orders/catalog_client.py:1-4,19-23`; `components/orders/test_catalog_client.py:37-62`). Orders computes totals, validates stock, and sends settlement requests to a partner or local development endpoint (`components/orders/orders.py:19-51`). The `bible-mode-b` queue uses GitHub issues, branches, and pull requests to assign Copilot work, inspect artifacts, and coordinate human review (`.github/bible/bible_queue.py:145-167,577-642,681-793`). The `tools` commands generate a component plan, validate component artifacts, and create component issues (`tools/plan.py:21-58`; `tools/gate.py:42-78`; `tools/fanout.sh:7-30`). GitHub Actions runs the queue and related automation on hosted Ubuntu runners; no production deployment topology for catalog or orders is declared (`.github/workflows/bible-queue.yml:19-37`; [`architecture`](hld/02-architecture.md)). The main operational cautions are plain-HTTP supplier and payment calls, unauthenticated catalog routes, process-local product data, and no source evidence for the supplier feed's claimed nightly schedule (`components/catalog/catalog.py:5,36-47`; `components/catalog/service.py:24-43`; `components/orders/orders.py:7-12,45-50`). A separate catalog–orders TLS migration is documented as planning only; its manifest remains at producer stage 0 (`tls-migration/tls-services.yaml:18-21`; [`cross-cutting concerns`](hld/06-cross-cutting.md#tls-migration-planning)).

## How to run

- One component: `python3 -I .github/skills/analyzing-a-codebase/scripts/next.py --repo . --analysis codebase-analysis --component NAME --new-session`, then follow what it prints until `COMPONENT DONE NAME`.
- Where every component stands: `python3 -I .github/skills/analyzing-a-codebase/scripts/next.py --repo . --analysis codebase-analysis --board`.
- On GitHub without workflows: one issue per component from `ledger/issues/` (docs/github-guide.md, Part 4).
- When every component is done: the assemble step (`ledger/issues/assemble.md`).

# Architecture

The application is a small Python library with a standard-library HTTP server; the repository also contains command-line analysis tools and GitHub Actions adapters. No application image, package build, deployment manifest, service manager, or production topology is declared. GitHub Actions runs the Mode B scripts on hosted `ubuntu-latest` runners. The TLS migration inventory and service configuration are repository configuration artifacts, not deployed services (`tls-migration/evidence/inventory.json:1-14`; `tls-migration/tls-services.yaml:1-20`).

## Record lifecycles

### GitHub issue

The queue creates an open issue, updates its body/labels/assignment while it is active, and closes it either as completed or not planned. A retry is a new issue with an incremented attempt, not a reopening of the failed issue.

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> Open : create_issue
  Open --> Open : assign, comment, label, update body
  Open --> ClosedCompleted : close(reason=completed)
  Open --> ClosedNotPlanned : fail or release
  ClosedCompleted --> [*]
  ClosedNotPlanned --> [*] : retry creates a new issue
```

| Element | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| `create_issue` starts tracker and session records | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:144-151,538-571,640-660` |

| Normal close reason defaults to `completed` | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:316-317` |
| Failed attempts close as `not_planned`; a later attempt is newly created | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:546-574` |

### Agent session pull request

Agent PRs are merged into a component branch after path and status checks; failed PRs are closed. The separate component review PR targets the default branch and is merged by a person, not by this queue.

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> Draft : Copilot opens session PR
  Draft --> Ready : ready(pr)
  Ready --> MergedToComponentBranch : merge(pr)
  Draft --> Closed : failure closes PR
  Ready --> Closed : failure closes PR
```

| Element | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Agent may open draft; queue marks it ready before merge | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:328-335` |
| Queue validates changed files and status before merging session PR | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:794-851` |
| Failed session closes its PR | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:546-565` |

### Component review pull request

The separate component review PR targets the default branch and is merged by a person, not by this queue.

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> ReviewOpen : create component PR
  ReviewOpen --> MergedByPerson : human merges to default branch
```

| Element | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Component review PR is opened for a person to review | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:707-711`; module docstring `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:28` |

The component status artifact also carries `NEW_CHAT`, `COMPONENT_DONE`, `WAITING_ANSWER`, and `STOP`; this repository code reads these values to decide queue behavior but does not write their transitions (`.github/bible/bible_queue.py:65-66,425-429,688-708`). The transitions belong to the analysis toolkit and are not inferred here.

| State | Reads | Writes | Lifecycle | Evidence |

| `plan.json` | Gate and fanout tools | Planning tool | Regenerated from component Python files | `tools/plan.py:21-58`; `tools/gate.py:86`; `tools/fanout.sh:9` |

| `components.json`, issue templates, status and verification reports | Queue reads from GitHub default or component branch | Queue changes GitHub issue/PR state, not these local files | Component artifacts move with their branches; whole-system files are read from the default branch | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:332-389,502-510,538-571,619-627,739-774` |
| `baseline.json` | Queue checks its presence before delta work | Not written by the queue | Missing baseline prevents delta issue creation | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1201-1205` |
| Changed-path list | `delta` reads one UTF-8 path per line | Workflow writes it to `$RUNNER_TEMP/changed.txt` | Removed with the runner workspace | `.github/workflows/bible-delta.yml:31-38`; `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1285-1288` |
| Gate tarball and extracted worktree | Coverage and status subprocesses | Queue streams and extracts under a temporary location | Temporary buffer closes; worktree is removed in `finally` | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:237-260,723-735` |
| POC `request.json`, `response.json` | `gh api` receives request file; `jq` reads response fields | POC job writes both in runner workspace | No checkout or repository commit; runner workspace is ephemeral | `.github/workflows/poc-assign-copilot.yml:55-69` |

# Key flows

| # | Flow | Trigger | Components | Endpoint cards |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Start an analysis run | Operator dispatches `bible-plan` | GitHub Actions, `bible_queue.py`, GitHub | None |
| 2 | Queue creates and assigns the planning session | Queue schedule or manual dispatch | `bible_queue.py`, GitHub, Copilot | None |
| 3 | Component session passes the gate and reaches human review | Agent session PR and `COMPONENT_DONE` status | Queue, toolkit gate, Copilot, reviewer | None |
| 4 | Whole-analysis assembly and verification | All component review PRs are merged | Queue, assembly agent, verification agent, reviewer | None |
| 5 | Changed code produces component delta issues | Default-branch push | Delta workflow, queue, GitHub, Copilot | None |
| 6 | Order total and stock validation use the in-process catalog | Python caller invokes order functions | `orders`, `catalog` | None |
| 7 | Remote catalog client reads a price | Python caller or HTTP client test | `catalog_client`, catalog HTTP service | [Catalog API](../lld/api/catalog/catalog.md) |
| 8 | Settlement sends an order amount | Python caller invokes `settle` | `orders`, payment partner or local fake | None |
| 9 | Component plan, fanout and gate | Local operator runs the tools | `plan.py`, `fanout.sh`, `gate.py`, GitHub CLI | None |
| 10 | POC workflow creates and assigns a task issue | Operator dispatches the POC workflow | GitHub Actions, `gh`, GitHub, Copilot | None |

## 1. Start an analysis run

**Trigger:** An operator dispatches `bible-plan` from the default branch. **Outcome:** The workflow creates one tracker issue with the run settings; the queue starts the planning session on its next run.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  actor Operator as Repository operator
  participant Actions as GitHub Actions
  participant Queue as bible_queue.py
  participant API as GitHub API
  Operator->>Actions: Dispatch bible-plan with model and component inputs
  Actions->>Queue: Run start with GH_TOKEN and workflow inputs
  Queue->>Queue: Validate model and component arguments
  Queue->>API: REST request, HTTPS :443 by default, ensure labels and create tracker issue
  API-->>Queue: HTTPS :443 by default, tracker issue number
  Queue-->>Actions: Print tracker number and queue-start guidance
  Actions-->>Operator: Report workflow result
```

| Step | What happens | Evidence |
| ---: | --- | --- |
| 1 | Operator dispatches the workflow and supplies the inputs. | `.github/workflows/bible-plan.yml:7-23` |
| 2 | Workflow checks the default branch, verifies `BIBLE_ASSIGN_TOKEN`, and invokes `start`. | `.github/workflows/bible-plan.yml:37-54` |
| 3 | `main` validates the model, component arguments, and settings. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1267-1279` |
| 4 | Queue ensures labels, refuses an already-open tracker, and creates a tracker issue with settings in a hidden JSON comment. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1272-1280` |
| 5 | GitHub returns the tracker issue number. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1280-1281` |
| 6 | CLI prints the issue number and queue-start guidance. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1281-1282` |
| 7 | Workflow reports its result to the operator. | `.github/workflows/bible-plan.yml:50-54` |

**Failure paths:** A non-default branch skips the job; missing secret exits with an error; invalid models, components, settings, missing repository/token settings, or an already-open tracker terminate `start` rather than creating a second run (`.github/workflows/bible-plan.yml:37-54`; `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1260-1279`).

heading_path: 2. Queue creates and assigns the planning session
text:
## 2. Queue creates and assigns the planning session

**Trigger:** The 15-minute schedule or a manual queue dispatch. **Outcome:** Reconciliation reads GitHub state and opens/assigns the next planning issue.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  participant Actions as GitHub Actions
  participant Queue as bible_queue.py
  participant API as GitHub API
  participant Agent as Copilot coding agent
  Actions->>Queue: Run reconcile from default-branch checkout
  Queue->>API: REST request, HTTPS :443 by default, list open tracker issues
  API-->>Queue: HTTPS :443 by default, tracker and hidden settings
  Queue->>Queue: Read components.json and select planning phase
  Queue->>API: REST request, HTTPS :443 by default, read planning issue text
  API-->>Queue: HTTPS :443 by default, issue template
  Queue->>API: REST request, HTTPS :443 by default, create planning issue
  Queue->>API: REST request, HTTPS :443 by default, assign configured model
  API-->>Agent: Deliver issue assignment
  Agent-->>API: Open planning PR
```

| Step | What happens | Evidence |
| ---: | --- | --- |
| 1 | The queue workflow starts on schedule or manual dispatch and checks out the default branch. | `.github/workflows/bible-queue.yml:7-10,23-37` |
| 2 | `reconcile` lists open tracker issues. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:129-131,486-488` |
| 3 | GitHub returns the tracker and its hidden settings. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:129-131,316-321` |
| 4 | Queue selects planning when `components.json` is missing, non-dict, marked proposed, or lacks a list-valued `components` field. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:601-603` |
| 5 | Queue reads the planning issue text from `ledger/issues/plan.md`. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:645-652` |
| 6 | GitHub returns the issue template. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:645-652` |
| 7 | Queue creates the planning issue. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:144-151,538-546` |
| 8 | Queue assigns the configured analysis model. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:144-151,341-345` |
| 9 | GitHub delivers the issue assignment to Copilot. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:160-167` |
| 10 | Agent work and PR status return through GitHub issue timelines and pull requests. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:195-220,404-429` |

**Failure paths:** An unreadable tracker settings block is logged and skipped; a per-tracker exception does not stop reconciliation of other trackers. A detected start error creates a human hold; a no-PR timeout retries once, then requires a person (`.github/bible/bible_queue.py:481-487,455-474`).

heading_path: 3. Component session passes the gate and reaches human review
text:
## 3. Component session passes the gate and reaches human review

**Trigger:** Component work produces a session PR and a `COMPONENT_DONE` status. **Outcome:** A matching clean verification opens a component review PR to the default branch.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  participant Agent as Copilot coding agent
  participant API as GitHub
  participant Queue as bible_queue.py
  participant Gate as coverage.py and status.py
  actor Reviewer as Repository reviewer
  Agent->>API: Open chunk PR with component pages and status
  Queue->>API: REST request, HTTPS :443 by default, read PR files and status
  Queue->>API: REST request, HTTPS :443 by default, merge accepted session PR
  Queue->>API: REST request, HTTPS :443 by default, read component status
  Queue->>API: HTTPS :443 by default, download component branch tarball
  Queue->>Gate: Check coverage and calculate page fingerprint
  Gate-->>Queue: Gate result and fingerprint
  Queue->>API: REST request, HTTPS :443 by default, create verification issue
  Agent->>API: Open verification PR with report
  Queue->>API: REST request, HTTPS :443 by default, read report and merge PR
  Queue->>API: REST request, HTTPS :443 by default, create component review PR
  Reviewer->>API: Review and merge component PR
```

| Step | What happens | Evidence |
| ---: | --- | --- |
| 1 | Queue observes the chunk or verification session and its linked PR. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:794-810` |
| 2 | Queue validates allowed file paths and reads status JSON at the PR head. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:814-847` |
| 3 | A valid session PR is merged and its issue is closed. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:848-851` |
| 4 | Queue reads component status; on `COMPONENT_DONE`, it starts the gate. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:731-741` |
| 5 | Queue unpacks the branch tarball in a temporary directory. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:264-303,859-865` |
| 6 | Queue runs coverage and fingerprint checks using scripts from the configured toolkit path. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:853-879` |
| 7 | Gate returns its pass/fail result and page fingerprint. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:866-873` |
| 8 | Queue starts a verification issue using the distinct verification model. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:785-792` |
| 9 | Verification PR must contain a report before it can be merged. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:845-847` |
| 10 | Queue reads the verification verdict and fingerprint after the session is merged. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:753-780` |
| 11 | A clean `PASS` whose fingerprint matches the checked pages creates a PR for a person to review. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:765-779` |
| 12 | Human reviewer merges the component PR to the default branch. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:28,608-612` |

**Failure paths:** Disallowed PR files, `STOP`, no progress, missing verification report, or a revision that does not reach `COMPONENT_DONE` triggers the one-retry/hold logic. `WAITING_ANSWER` labels the issue and PR. A failed gate starts more component work; a report with corrections, an unreadable or stale fingerprint, or repeated non-clean verification leads to revision, re-verification, or a human hold (`.github/bible/bible_queue.py:455-483,659-713,608-627`).

## 4. Whole-analysis assembly and verification

**Trigger:** Component review PRs have been merged. **Outcome:** Assembly and a second-model verification are merged; a clean whole-analysis report closes the tracker.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  actor Reviewer as Repository reviewer
  participant Actions as GitHub Actions
  participant Queue as bible_queue.py
  participant API as GitHub
  participant Agent as Copilot coding agent
  Reviewer->>API: Merge all component review PRs
  Actions->>Queue: Run scheduled reconcile
  Queue->>Queue: Select whole-system assembly phase
  Queue->>API: REST request, HTTPS :443 by default, read assembly issue template
  API-->>Queue: HTTPS :443 by default, assembly template
  Queue->>API: REST request, HTTPS :443 by default, create and assign issue
  Agent->>API: Open assembly PR with whole-system pages
  Reviewer->>API: Review and merge assembly PR
  Queue->>API: REST request, HTTPS :443 by default, close assembly and create verify-all issue
  Agent->>API: Open verification PR with whole-analysis report
  Reviewer->>API: Review and merge verification PR
  Queue->>API: REST request, HTTPS :443 by default, read verdict and report
  Queue->>API: REST request, HTTPS :443 by default, close tracker after clean PASS
```

| Step | What happens | Evidence |
| ---: | --- | --- |
| 1 | Component PRs are merged by a person; scripts do not merge work to the default branch. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:28,608-612` |
| 2 | Queue workflow invokes reconciliation. | `.github/workflows/bible-queue.yml:7-10,23-37` |
| 3 | Queue selects the whole-system assembly phase. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:779-783` |
| 4 | Queue reads the assembly issue template. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:332-338,765-766` |
| 5 | GitHub returns the assembly template. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:409-415` |
| 6 | Queue creates and assigns the assembly issue. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1006-1008` |
| 7 | Assembly agent opens a PR with whole-system pages. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:404-409,765-772`; `ledger/issues/assemble.md` |
| 8 | A person reviews and merges the assembly PR to the default branch. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:787-795` |
| 9 | Queue closes the assembly issue and creates a verification issue using `verify_model`. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:746-754,768-773` |
| 10 | Verification agent opens a PR with the whole-analysis report. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:404-409,768-772` |
| 11 | A person reviews and merges the verification PR. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:787-795` |
| 12 | Queue reads the report and requires `PASS` with no major corrections. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:790-794` |
| 13 | Queue closes the tracker and posts `Done`. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1014-1015` |

**Failure paths:** If whole verification is missing, unreadable, not `PASS`, or has major corrections, the queue returns a human-needed message rather than closing the tracker. If the assembly or verification session is held or fails to start, it reports that state and follows the retry/hold rules (`.github/bible/bible_queue.py:455-483,749-770`).

heading_path: 5. Changed code produces component delta issues
text:
## 5. Changed code produces component delta issues

**Trigger:** A push on the default branch that changes files outside the ignored paths. **Outcome:** Queue maps changed paths to components and creates one update issue per affected component.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  participant Git as GitHub push event
  participant Actions as GitHub Actions
  participant Queue as bible_queue.py
  participant API as GitHub API
  participant Agent as Copilot coding agent
  Git->>Actions: Push on default branch
  Actions->>Actions: Checkout full history and write changed.txt
  Actions->>Queue: Run delta with changed-file path
  Queue->>API: REST request, HTTPS :443 by default, read components and baseline
  Queue->>Queue: Map changed source paths to component names
  Queue->>API: REST request, HTTPS :443 by default, skip duplicate or create delta issue
  API-->>Agent: Assign new issue
```

| Step | What happens | Evidence |
| ---: | --- | --- |
| 1 | Push workflow runs only for default-branch changes and ignores `.github/**` and `codebase-analysis/**`. | `.github/workflows/bible-delta.yml:6-10,18-20` |
| 2 | Workflow checks out full history and writes changed paths to `$RUNNER_TEMP/changed.txt`. | `.github/workflows/bible-delta.yml:21-23,29-36` |
| 3 | CLI reads nonempty path lines and passes them to `Queue.delta`. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1285-1290` |
| 4 | Queue requires `components.json` and `ledger/baseline.json`. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1201-1205` |
| 5 | Queue maps changed source paths to component names. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:839-846` |
| 6 | Queue skips a duplicate open delta issue or creates a new issue. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:846-858` |
| 7 | GitHub assigns each newly created issue to Copilot. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:849-857` |

**Failure paths:** The first push with no prior SHA exits without a delta run. Missing catalog or baseline makes the queue log that there is nothing to update. Empty paths or paths outside component ownership produce no issue; an already-open delta issue is not duplicated (`.github/workflows/bible-delta.yml:31-38`; `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:835-858`).

heading_path: 6. Order total and stock validation use the in-process catalog
text:
## 6. Order total and stock validation use the in-process catalog

**Trigger:** Python caller invokes `order_total` and `validate`. **Outcome:** The caller receives a rounded total and a list of quantity/stock errors; no order or stock reservation is persisted.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  participant Caller as Python caller
  participant Orders as orders.py
  participant Catalog as catalog.py
  Caller->>Orders: order_total(lines, loyal)
  loop each order line
    Orders->>Catalog: price_of(sku)
    Catalog-->>Orders: unit price
  end
  Orders-->>Caller: rounded total using larger discount
  Caller->>Orders: validate(lines)
  loop each line
    Orders->>Catalog: in_stock(sku, qty)
    Catalog-->>Orders: true or false
  end
  Orders-->>Caller: error list
```

| Step | What happens | Evidence |
| ---: | --- | --- |
| 1 | Caller supplies `(sku, qty)` lines and a loyalty flag. | `components/orders/orders.py:23-24` |
| 2 | `order_total` requests each line's price from `catalog.price_of`. | `components/orders/orders.py:19-25` |
| 3 | Catalog returns the price for a known SKU. | `components/catalog/catalog.py:20-25` |
| 4 | `order_total` selects the larger loyalty/bulk discount and returns the rounded total. | `components/orders/orders.py:14-16,26-32` |
| 5 | Caller invokes `validate` on the lines. | `components/orders/orders.py:35` |
| 6 | Validation rejects nonpositive quantities or asks the catalog whether stock is sufficient. | `components/orders/orders.py:35-42` |
| 7 | Catalog returns stock availability for the SKU. | `components/catalog/catalog.py:27-29` |
| 8 | Validation returns one error string per invalid line; no stock is decremented or order record written. | `components/orders/orders.py:35-42` |

**Failure paths:** Unknown SKU raises `KeyError` during total calculation. Validation accumulates `"quantity must be positive"` or `"not enough stock"` errors for invalid lines (`components/catalog/catalog.py:20-29`; `components/orders/orders.py:23-42`).

heading_path: 7. Remote catalog client reads a price
text:
## 7. Remote catalog client reads a price

**Trigger:** Caller uses `remote_price` or `remote_line_total`; the repository's test starts the catalog service on loopback. **Outcome:** Client reads the JSON price and converts it to a float.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  participant Client as catalog_client.py
  participant Server as CatalogHandler
  participant Catalog as catalog.py
  Client->>Client: Read CATALOG_URL and percent-encode SKU
  Client->>Server: GET /price/sku, HTTP port 8001 by default or ephemeral in test
  Server->>Server: Decode URL path
  Server->>Catalog: price_of(sku)
  Catalog-->>Server: Price or KeyError
  Server-->>Client: 200 JSON price or 404 JSON error
  Client-->>Client: Parse response price as float
```

| Step | What happens | Evidence |
| ---: | --- | --- |
| 1 | Client reads `CATALOG_URL` and quotes the SKU. | `components/orders/catalog_client.py:11,14-21` |
| 2 | Client sends GET with its configured timeout (default 5 seconds). | `components/orders/catalog_client.py:19-23` |
| 3 | Handler extracts the URL path. | `components/catalog/service.py:24-25` |
| 4 | Handler decodes the SKU and calls `price_of`. | `components/catalog/service.py:28-30` |
| 5 | Catalog returns a price or raises `KeyError` for an unknown SKU. | `components/catalog/catalog.py:20-24` |
| 6 | Server returns `200` with `sku` and `price`, or `404` with an error. | `components/catalog/service.py:28-34` |
| 7 | Client loads the JSON body and converts `price` to `float`. | `components/orders/catalog_client.py:22-23` |

**Failure paths:** Unknown SKUs return 404, which `urlopen` surfaces as `HTTPError`; invalid JSON, missing fields, timeouts, and connection errors are not translated by the client. The HTTP client path has test callers only in this repository (`components/orders/catalog_client.py:19-23`; `components/orders/test_catalog_client.py:37-62`).

## 8. Settlement sends an order amount

**Trigger:** Python caller invokes `settle(order_id, amount, dev=False)`. **Outcome:** It sends JSON and returns whether a received response has status 200.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  participant Caller as Python caller
  participant Orders as orders.py
  participant Partner as Payment partner or dev fake
  Caller->>Orders: settle(order_id, amount, dev)
  Orders->>Orders: Select partner or localhost URL
  Orders->>Orders: Serialize order and amount as JSON
  Orders->>Partner: POST JSON, HTTP port 80 implicit
  Partner-->>Orders: HTTP response from port 80
  Orders-->>Caller: true only for status 200
```

| Step | What happens | Evidence |
| ---: | --- | --- |
| 1 | Caller supplies the order identifier, amount, and optional development flag. | `components/orders/orders.py:45` |
| 2 | `dev=True` selects `localhost:8099`; otherwise the hard-coded partner URL is used. | `components/orders/orders.py:7-12,47` |
| 3 | Code serializes `order` and `amount` as JSON. | `components/orders/orders.py:48-49` |
| 4 | Code sends the POST with a 15-second timeout by default. | `components/orders/orders.py:49-50` |
| 5 | Partner returns an HTTP response. | `components/orders/orders.py:49-51` |
| 6 | Function returns whether the response status equals 200. | `components/orders/orders.py:50-51` |

**Failure paths:** Network and HTTP errors from `urlopen` propagate; a non-200 response that is returned yields `False`. No retry or idempotency key is shown (`components/orders/orders.py:45-51`).

## 9. Component plan, fanout and gate

**Trigger:** Local operator runs the planning command and then fans out issues; the gate is run for a component pass. **Outcome:** Plan JSON is generated, issues are opened, and each gate reports pass/failure.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  actor Operator as Local operator
  participant Plan as tools/plan.py
  participant Files as Repository files
  participant Fanout as tools/fanout.sh
  participant GH as GitHub CLI
  participant Gate as tools/gate.py
  Operator->>Plan: Run planner
  Plan->>Files: Read component Python files and tests
  Plan->>Files: Write codebase-analysis/plan.json
  Operator->>Fanout: Run with owner/repo and ENGINE
  Fanout->>Files: Read component names from plan.json
  Fanout->>GH: Create labels and component issues
  Operator->>Gate: Run selected component pass
  Gate->>Files: Read plan and component artifacts
  Gate->>Files: Run unittest discovery for pass 3
  Gate-->>Operator: Print PASS or FAIL
```

| Step | What happens | Evidence |
| ---: | --- | --- |
| 1 | Operator runs the planner. | `tools/plan.py:41-62` |
| 2 | Planner scans component Python files, functions, tests, and literal HTTP URLs. | `tools/plan.py:21-38` |
| 3 | Planner writes versioned JSON to `codebase-analysis/plan.json`. | `tools/plan.py:41-58` |
| 4 | Operator runs fanout with a repository and engine selection. | `tools/fanout.sh:2-8` |
| 5 | Fanout reads component names from `plan.json`. | `tools/fanout.sh:9` |
| 6 | Fanout creates labels and issues through `gh`. | `tools/fanout.sh:10-29` |
| 7 | Operator runs the component gate for a selected pass. | `tools/gate.py:81-92` |
| 8 | Gate reads the plan and component pass artifacts. | `tools/gate.py:42-65,86-108` |
| 9 | For pass 3, gate invokes unittest discovery. | `tools/gate.py:63-78` |
| 10 | Gate prints PASS/FAIL and returns its process status. | `tools/gate.py:23-26,109-117` |

**Failure paths:** File/AST/JSON errors stop the relevant tool; the gate fails on missing artifacts, unresolved `ASK`, no new test functions, or failing tests. `fanout.sh` exits on command failure and rejects an unknown engine (`tools/plan.py:21-58`; `tools/gate.py:42-78,94-108`; `tools/fanout.sh:6,24-30`).

## 10. POC workflow creates and assigns a task issue

**Trigger:** Operator dispatches the standalone POC workflow. **Outcome:** A GitHub issue is created and assigned directly to Copilot; the workflow does not check out repository code.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  actor Operator as Repository operator
  participant Actions as GitHub Actions
  participant Shell as POC shell and jq
  participant API as GitHub Issues API
  participant Agent as Copilot coding agent
  Operator->>Actions: Dispatch title, task, base and model
  Actions->>Shell: Pass inputs and secret through environment
  Shell->>Shell: Exit if secret is missing
  Shell->>Shell: Build request.json without token
  Shell->>API: gh api POST issue, HTTPS :443 by default
  API-->>Shell: HTTPS :443 by default, issue response
  Shell->>Shell: Write response.json and print issue details
  API-->>Agent: Assign issue to Copilot
```

| Step | What happens | Evidence |
| ---: | --- | --- |
| 1 | Operator supplies required title, task, base branch and optional model. | `.github/workflows/poc-assign-copilot.yml:11-29` |
| 2 | Workflow passes input values and `BIBLE_ASSIGN_TOKEN` into environment variables; the job performs no checkout. | `.github/workflows/poc-assign-copilot.yml:34-48` |
| 3 | Shell exits if the token is missing. | `.github/workflows/poc-assign-copilot.yml:49-53` |
| 4 | `jq` creates `request.json` with issue body, assignee and `agent_assignment`; the token is not included in the JSON payload. | `.github/workflows/poc-assign-copilot.yml:55-64` |
| 5 | `gh api` creates the issue. | `.github/workflows/poc-assign-copilot.yml:65-68` |
| 6 | GitHub returns the issue response. | `.github/workflows/poc-assign-copilot.yml:65-68` |
| 7 | Shell writes `response.json` and prints issue details. | `.github/workflows/poc-assign-copilot.yml:68-72` |
| 8 | GitHub assigns the issue to Copilot. | `.github/workflows/poc-assign-copilot.yml:65-72` |

**Failure paths:** Missing `BIBLE_ASSIGN_TOKEN` exits before request creation; invalid input or API/CLI errors stop the job under `set -euo pipefail`. No retry or timeout is specified (`.github/workflows/poc-assign-copilot.yml:40-69`).

# Cross-cutting concerns

## Authentication and authorisation

The GitHub automation authenticates API requests with a bearer token; the catalog and sample order endpoints have no application authentication. The workflow jobs are restricted to the default branch where specified and declare `contents: read`, while the separate assignment token's repository permissions are configured outside this repository.

| Component | How | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bible-mode-b` | Uses `GH_TOKEN` in the GitHub API `Authorization` header. Plan, queue and delta workflows take it from `BIBLE_ASSIGN_TOKEN` and check out the default branch before running the queue code. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:105-119`; `.github/workflows/bible-plan.yml:26-45`; `.github/workflows/bible-queue.yml:12-36`; `.github/workflows/bible-delta.yml:14-33` |
| POC assignment | Uses `BIBLE_ASSIGN_TOKEN` as `GH_TOKEN`; the workflow creates the issue through `gh api`. The workflow declares `contents: read` and performs no checkout. | `.github/workflows/poc-assign-copilot.yml:4-8,31-46,66-69` |
| `catalog` | HTTP handlers do not authenticate requests. The server defaults to loopback, but `CATALOG_HOST` can change the bind address. | `components/catalog/service.py:15-34,40-43` |
| `orders` | Settlement and remote catalog requests use plain HTTP; no client credentials or authorization headers are set. | `components/orders/orders.py:7-12,45-50`; `components/orders/catalog_client.py:19-23` |

Consistency: varies (4 variants)

## Secrets

The workflow token is passed to the process through an environment variable, not embedded in workflow source or the issue request payload. The repository code refers to secret names only; the secret value and its provisioning are external.

| Component | How | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bible-mode-b` | Workflows map `secrets.BIBLE_ASSIGN_TOKEN` to `GH_TOKEN`, check it before running, and the API client sends it as a bearer token. | `.github/workflows/bible-plan.yml:43-53`; `.github/workflows/bible-queue.yml:31-37`; `.github/workflows/bible-delta.yml:26-38`; `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:115-119` |
| POC assignment | Shell checks the token; `jq` constructs `request.json` from input values and does not add the token to that JSON. | `.github/workflows/poc-assign-copilot.yml:40-63` |
| Sample application | No application secrets or credential configuration are shown in the catalog or orders modules. | `components/catalog/catalog.py:1-47`; `components/catalog/service.py:1-49`; `components/orders/orders.py:1-51`; `components/orders/catalog_client.py:1-29` |

Consistency: varies (3 variants)

## Configuration

Configuration is split across workflow inputs, environment variables, and source constants; no environment profile or central settings service is declared. The architecture page's configuration table lists the known settings and defaults.

| Component | How | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bible-mode-b` | Workflow inputs select components, models and concurrency; environment variables configure GitHub API access, toolkit location, and optional clock/test settings. | `.github/workflows/bible-plan.yml:9-24,44-49`; `.github/workflows/bible-queue.yml:31-37`; `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:34-36,60-64,91,307-309,397-399` |
| `catalog` | Bind address and port use `CATALOG_HOST` and `CATALOG_PORT`; supplier and image URLs are constants. | `components/catalog/service.py:40-43`; `components/catalog/catalog.py:5-6` |
| `orders` | Catalog base URL uses `CATALOG_URL`; settlement URLs, discounts, bulk threshold and request timeout are function defaults or constants. | `components/orders/catalog_client.py:11,14-23`; `components/orders/orders.py:7-16,45-50` |
| `tools` | Fanout reads `ENGINE` with default `copilot`; plan and gate paths are repository-local. | `tools/fanout.sh:2-12,24-29`; `tools/plan.py:41-58`; `tools/gate.py:81-108` |

Consistency: varies (4 variants)

## TLS migration planning

The repository includes a local catalog–orders TLS migration plan, but it is planning-only: the manifest has `migrator_model: null` and `producer.stage: 0`, and the plan explicitly says that no migration artifacts or gate results have been created (`tls-migration/tls-services.yaml:1-4,18-26`; `tls-migration/02-certificate-plan.md:1-4,45-53`). The inventory identifies the catalog HTTP listener and separate-service orders client as intended migration targets while excluding the supplier and payment calls (`tls-migration/01-inventory.md:8-14,18-33`). This plan does not describe deployed TLS behavior; the current catalog handler and orders HTTP client remain the runtime source of truth (`components/catalog/service.py:24-43`; `components/orders/catalog_client.py:11-23`).

Consistency: planning only; no runtime TLS implementation is evidenced.

## Error handling and resilience

The sample modules generally expose network and data errors to callers; the queue translates GitHub request failures and isolates reconciliation errors per tracker. Session failures get one retry before a human hold, but network requests have no general retry policy.

| Component | How | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `catalog` | Unknown products raise `KeyError` in `price_of`; the HTTP handler returns 404 for that error. Supplier-fetch errors and feed parsing errors are not caught here. | `components/catalog/catalog.py:20-24,36-39,42-47`; `components/catalog/service.py:28-34` |
| `orders` | Validation returns per-line errors; unknown SKUs in totals and HTTP/transport errors from settlement or remote price lookup propagate to the caller. | `components/orders/orders.py:23-42,45-51`; `components/orders/catalog_client.py:19-23` |
| `bible-mode-b` | GitHub HTTP and transport errors become `RuntimeError`; reconciliation catches an exception per tracker. Failed agent work is retried once, then labelled for human attention. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:105-117,485-496,464-483` |
| `tools` | Gate reports missing or invalid artifacts and failing tests as failures; shell fanout stops on command errors. | `tools/gate.py:42-78,94-117`; `tools/fanout.sh:6,24-30` |

Request timeouts are explicit for GitHub API calls (60 seconds by default, with a 300-second tarball timeout), catalog price lookup (5 seconds), settlement (15 seconds), and supplier feed (10 seconds). There are no retries around these request calls; the queue's one retry is for failed agent sessions, not network requests (`.github/bible/bible_queue.py:94-103,464-483`; `components/orders/catalog_client.py:19-23`; `components/orders/orders.py:45-50`; `components/catalog/catalog.py:36-39`).

Consistency: varies (4 variants)

## Logging, metrics, and tracing

The queue writes progress and error messages to standard output; the catalog HTTP server suppresses its request log messages. No metrics or distributed tracing mechanism is present in the inspected source and workflow configuration.

| Component | How | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bible-mode-b` | Queue defaults its logging callback to `print` and emits tracker and gate status. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:396-399,491-496,721-729,780-788` |
| `catalog` | `CatalogHandler.log_message` is a no-op. | `components/catalog/service.py:36-37` |
| Sample application and tools | No logging framework, metrics, or tracing calls were found in the repository sweep. | `codebase-analysis/progress.md` (Sweep: Outbound Python, Entry points, and Security dispositions) |

Consistency: varies (2 variants)

## Build, deployment, and dependencies

The sample application and tools run from source without a declared package build; GitHub Actions uses hosted Ubuntu runners. The repository's application and queue code use Python's standard library, while workflows also invoke GitHub Actions, `gh`, and `jq`.

| Component | How | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `catalog` and `orders` | Python source modules; the catalog server is started with `python3 -m components.catalog.service`. No application packaging or deployment manifest is identified in the component pages. | `components/catalog/service.py:1-12,40-49`; `components/orders/orders.py:1-5`; `codebase-analysis/lld/catalog/README.md`; `codebase-analysis/lld/orders/README.md` |
| `bible-mode-b` | Python queue runs on `ubuntu-latest` after checkout; workflow job timeouts and concurrency are defined in YAML. | `.github/workflows/bible-plan.yml:29-40`; `.github/workflows/bible-queue.yml:15-30`; `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1244-1262` |
| `tools` | Python scripts and Bash run from the repository; fanout invokes `gh`. | `tools/plan.py:41-62`; `tools/gate.py:81-117`; `tools/fanout.sh:1-31` |

Consistency: varies (3 variants)

## Testing

The sample components use Python's `unittest`; the tool gate runs discovery for pass 3. No repository Actions workflow in the inventory invokes that test command automatically.

| Component | How | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `catalog` and `orders` | Tests are `unittest.TestCase` modules; orders' catalog-client tests start a local HTTP server. | `components/catalog/test_catalog.py:1-12`; `components/orders/test_orders.py:1-12`; `components/orders/test_catalog_client.py:1-66` |
| `tools` | Pass 3 of the gate invokes `python -m unittest discover`. | `tools/gate.py:63-78` |
| `bible-mode-b` | Workflows run the queue, plan or delta command; none invokes the application test suite. | `.github/workflows/bible-plan.yml:50-54`; `.github/workflows/bible-queue.yml:31-37`; `.github/workflows/bible-delta.yml:26-38` |

Consistency: varies (3 variants)

# bible-mode-b test: agent context

Generated from the analysis snapshot of 2026-11-23, depth deep. The code is the source of truth: open the cited lines before acting on any statement here.

Limits: Calls through dynamic dispatch, callbacks, reflection, string-built names, or another language may not appear in the graph; an absent `CALLS` edge is not proof of no call. `name-unique` and `analysis` edges depend on their resolution and the analysis, so treat them as leads to check. The graph and chunks describe this snapshot; after code changes, refresh the inventory, revise affected pages, and rerun `knowledge.py` (`.github/skills/analyzing-a-codebase/references/knowledge.md`).

## What the system is

The sample catalog/orders application sits beside GitHub Actions tooling that helps repository maintainers create and verify component analyses (`README.md:1-7`; `.github/workflows/bible-plan.yml:7-8`). Repository operators dispatch runs and reviewers inspect pull requests or answer issues; no customer audience for the sample app is declared (`.github/workflows/bible-plan.yml:7-8`; `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:590-642,681-793`). The four components are catalog, orders, `bible-mode-b`, and tools: they provide product lookups/orders, analysis queueing, and planning/gate/fanout functions (`components/catalog/catalog.py:15-47`; `components/orders/orders.py:19-51`; `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1244-1294`; `tools/plan.py:21-62`; `tools/gate.py:42-117`; `tools/fanout.sh:1-31`). The catalog has an optional loopback HTTP server; queue jobs run in GitHub Actions on hosted Ubuntu runners, and tools expose local CLI/shell entry points (`components/catalog/service.py:40-49`; `.github/workflows/bible-queue.yml:19-37`; `tools/plan.py:41-62`; `tools/gate.py:81-117`; `tools/fanout.sh:1-31`). Product data is process-local, orders has no durable order store, and queue state lives in GitHub issues, labels, branches, and pull requests (`components/catalog/catalog.py:8-12`; `components/orders/orders.py:45-51`; `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:145-167,305-325,590-642`).

## Components

| Component | Responsibility | Entry points | Key files | Page |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `catalog` | Owns process-local product data, price and stock lookups, supplier-feed helpers, and an optional HTTP API. | `python3 -m components.catalog.service`; `CatalogHandler.do_GET` (`components/catalog/service.py:24-49`) | `components/catalog/catalog.py`, `components/catalog/service.py` | `lld/catalog/README.md` |
| `orders` | Calculates line/order totals, validates stock, sends settlement requests, and has an optional remote catalog client. | Imported functions `line_total`, `order_total`, `validate`, `settle` (`components/orders/orders.py:19-51`) | `components/orders/orders.py`, `components/orders/catalog_client.py` | `lld/orders/README.md` |
| `bible-mode-b` | Starts and reconciles analysis runs, assigns agent issues, validates session results, opens human review PRs, and handles delta updates. | `start`, `reconcile`, `delta` commands (`.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1244-1294`) | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py`; workflow adapters in `.github/workflows/` | `lld/bible-mode-b/README.md` |
| `tools` | Generates a component plan, checks component artifacts/tests, and fans out component issues. | `python tools/plan.py`, `python tools/gate.py`, `tools/fanout.sh` (`tools/plan.py:41-62`; `tools/gate.py:81-117`; `tools/fanout.sh:1-31`) | `tools/plan.py`, `tools/gate.py`, `tools/fanout.sh` | `lld/tools/README.md` |

## Where to look

| To find | Look in |
| --- | --- |
| Catalog function or HTTP route behavior | `lld/catalog/catalog.md`, `lld/catalog/service.md`, and `lld/api/catalog/catalog.md` |
| Order total, stock, settlement, or remote price behavior | `lld/orders/orders.md` and `lld/orders/catalog_client.md` |
| Queue logic, state, and GitHub API calls | `lld/bible-mode-b/bible_queue.md`; use `hld/05-key-flows.md` for end-to-end sequence |
| Plan, gate, or fanout behavior | `lld/tools/plan.md`, `lld/tools/gate.md`, and `lld/tools/fanout.md` |
| Meaning and ownership of workflow data | `lld/data-dictionary.md` and `hld/04-data-architecture.md` |
| A function's callers and source facts | `knowledge/symbol-index.json`, `knowledge/graph.json`, then the cited function card and code |
| Settings, defaults, and secret names | `reference/configuration.md` |
| System architecture, outbound calls, or failure modes | `hld/01-system-context.md` through `hld/06-cross-cutting.md` |

## Domain vocabulary

- **SKU:** Product identifier and `_PRODUCTS` dictionary key (`components/catalog/catalog.py:8-12,15-17`).
- **Product feed:** Supplier JSON response consumed by `fetch_supplier_feed` and `apply_feed` (`components/catalog/catalog.py:36-47`).
- **In-process catalog access:** Current order path via `components.orders.catalog` (`components/orders/orders.py:5,19-20,35-42`).
- **Remote catalog client:** Optional HTTP price lookup for a separately deployed orders service (`components/orders/catalog_client.py:1-4,19-23`).
- **Loyalty discount:** Five-percent discount selected for a loyal order (`components/orders/orders.py:14,27-29`).
- **Bulk discount:** Ten-percent discount applied at total quantity 10 or more, not stacked with loyalty discount (`components/orders/orders.py:15-16,26-32`).
- **Analysis tracker:** GitHub issue storing the settings and state for one analysis run (`.github/bible/bible_queue.py:316-321,851-855`).
- **Agent session issue:** GitHub issue assigned to Copilot for one analysis or verification session (`.github/bible/bible_queue.py:144-151,538-546,771-773`).
- **Component branch:** Branch named `bible/<component>` holding component analysis work (`.github/bible/bible_queue.py:660-665`).
- **Session PR:** Agent-created pull request whose files and status are checked before the queue merges it into a component branch (`.github/bible/bible_queue.py:404-429,659-715`).
- **Component review PR:** Pull request from a completed component branch to the default branch for a person to review (`.github/bible/bible_queue.py:641-657`).
- **Pages fingerprint:** Value used to ensure a verification report refers to the current component pages (`.github/bible/bible_queue.py:609-623,707-709`).
- **Component plan:** `plan.json`, a versioned inventory of the files, tests, functions, and HTTP sites found for each component (`tools/plan.py:21-58`).
- **Component gate:** `gate.py` validation of analysis artifacts and pass-3 test results (`tools/gate.py:42-78,81-117`).
- **Issue fanout:** `fanout.sh` labels and creates one analysis issue per component in the plan (`tools/fanout.sh:7-30`).
- **Delta issue:** Follow-up issue for a component changed since the saved code-analysis baseline (`.github/bible/bible_queue.py:831-858`).
## Rules the code enforces

### Catalog

1. A price lookup for an unknown SKU raises `KeyError` (`components/catalog/catalog.py:20-24`).
2. Stock is sufficient only when a product exists and its stock is at least the requested quantity (`components/catalog/catalog.py:27-29`).
3. Supplier feed updates affect known SKUs only; absent `products` means no updates (`components/catalog/catalog.py:42-47`).
4. `GET /health` returns the health response with status 200 (`components/catalog/service.py:24-27`).
5. Unknown catalog GET paths return a 404 response (`components/catalog/service.py:33-34`).

### Orders

6. `validate` reports a quantity error for each nonpositive line quantity (`components/orders/orders.py:35-42`).
7. A positive quantity is valid only when catalog stock is sufficient (`components/orders/orders.py:37-42`; `components/catalog/catalog.py:27-29`).
8. Loyal orders use the loyalty discount unless a larger bulk discount applies (`components/orders/orders.py:14-16,23-32`).
9. `remote_line_total` rejects zero or negative quantities with `ValueError` (`components/orders/catalog_client.py:26-29`).
10. `settle` returns true only for an HTTP response with status 200 (`components/orders/orders.py:45-51`).

### Analysis queue

11. A run requires a nonempty verification model different from the analysis model (`.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1247-1268`).
12. Component selection must be `all` or valid comma-separated component names (`.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1269-1271`).
13. A new tracker cannot start while another tracker is open (`.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1272-1274`).
14. A failed agent session gets one retry; a second failure is labelled for human attention and unassigned (`.github/bible/bible_queue.py:555-574`).
15. Chunk and verification PRs may modify only their allowed analysis paths; disallowed files fail the session (`.github/bible/bible_queue.py:814-823`).
16. A component review PR requires a clean `PASS` and a matching nonempty page fingerprint (`.github/bible/bible_queue.py:641-657`).
17. Repeated verification without a clean matching pass leads to a human hold (`.github/bible/bible_queue.py:648-663`).

### Component tools

18. Pass 1 requires `inventory.md` to mention every function in the plan (`tools/gate.py:45-50`).
19. Pass 2 requires every planned HTTP site to be classified `CHANGE` or `KEEP`, with no unresolved `ASK` (`tools/gate.py:51-62`).
20. Pass 3 requires a tests report, an increased count of test functions since plan time, and successful unittest discovery (`tools/gate.py:63-78`).

## Conventions

The sample application and queue are Python modules using the standard library; the analysis toolchain adds Bash and GitHub Actions YAML, with no application package build or production deployment declared (`components/catalog/service.py:7-12`; `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1-10`; `tools/fanout.sh:1-6`; `hld/02-architecture.md`). Existing tests use `unittest`; the tool gate runs discovery only during component-analysis pass 3, not as a general workflow step (`components/catalog/test_catalog.py:1-12`; `components/orders/test_orders.py:1-12`; `tools/gate.py:63-78`; `.github/workflows/bible-queue.yml:31-37`).

Catalog products are mutable module memory; there is no durable application-side order record. Do not assume process restart persistence or a scheduled feed refresh (`components/catalog/catalog.py:8-12,36-47`; `components/orders/orders.py:45-51`; `hld/04-data-architecture.md`). Orders uses direct catalog calls in the current in-process mode; use `catalog_client.py` only for the documented separate-service path, not as an assumed current caller (`components/orders/orders.py:5,19-20,35-42`; `components/orders/catalog_client.py:1-4,19-23`).

The queue's durable run state is in GitHub issues, labels, branches, and PRs. Workflow jobs check out the default branch, and queue validations inspect component-branch files as data; do not make a PR's code the queue's gate implementation (`.github/workflows/bible-queue.yml:26-30`; `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:853-879`). `tools.plan.py` generates the component plan, `tools.gate.py` reads component artifacts, and `tools.fanout.sh` creates issues; the queue's delta command instead reads `components.json` and a changed-path file (`tools/plan.py:41-58`; `tools/gate.py:42-108`; `tools/fanout.sh:7-30`; `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1181-1241`).

Configuration is mostly environment variables, workflow inputs, and source constants; keep secret values out of files and issue payloads. Workflows map the repository secret `BIBLE_ASSIGN_TOKEN` to `GH_TOKEN`, and the queue sends that value as a bearer token (`.github/workflows/bible-plan.yml:43-53`; `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:105-119`). Use `reference/configuration.md` for all names/defaults; use `hld/03-integrations.md` for protocols, endpoints, authentication, and timeouts.

Errors are not handled uniformly. The catalog HTTP handler maps unknown price SKUs to 404, while direct price lookup raises `KeyError`; the order client and settlement functions generally let network exceptions reach callers (`components/catalog/catalog.py:20-24`; `components/catalog/service.py:28-34`; `components/orders/catalog_client.py:19-23`; `components/orders/orders.py:45-51`). The queue converts GitHub request errors to `RuntimeError`, catches exceptions per tracker, and retries agent sessions once (`.github/bible/bible_queue.py:105-117,485-496,464-483`). Keep these caller-visible behaviors in mind when changing error handling.

Logging is basic: the queue defaults to `print`, the gate prints pass/failure messages, and the catalog HTTP handler suppresses request logs; no metrics or tracing are implemented (`.github/bible/bible_queue.py:474-476`; `tools/gate.py:109-113`; `components/catalog/service.py:36-37`; `hld/06-cross-cutting.md`). Network operations use explicit timeouts but have no general network retry policy (`.github/bible/bible_queue.py:94-117,237-243`; `components/catalog/catalog.py:36-39`; `components/orders/catalog_client.py:19-23`; `components/orders/orders.py:45-50`).

## Hazards

- Settlement, supplier, and remote catalog traffic use plain HTTP; the catalog handlers do not authenticate, and `CATALOG_HOST` can bind beyond loopback. Review deployment and security requirements before exposing these paths (`components/orders/orders.py:7-12,45-50`; `components/catalog/catalog.py:5,36-39`; `components/orders/catalog_client.py:11,19-23`; `components/catalog/service.py:15-43`; `reference/risks-and-surprises.md`).
- Product records live only in memory. Feed entries for unknown SKUs are ignored; missing fields or failed numeric conversions can raise during `apply_feed` (`components/catalog/catalog.py:8-12,42-47`).
- A docstring says the supplier fetch runs nightly from cron, but no scheduler or caller is present in the repository. Do not add assumptions about refresh cadence (`components/catalog/catalog.py:36-39`; `progress.md`, Sweep: Scheduled/background work).
- The order tests do not exercise `order_total`, `validate`, or `settle`; existing test success does not establish those functions' behavior (`components/orders/test_orders.py:6-8`; `components/orders/test_catalog_client.py:37-62`).
- The queue API has no general retry; temporary GitHub failures can stop the current operation. Its agent retry is a distinct workflow rule (`.github/bible/bible_queue.py:94-117,464-483`).
- The queue source extends through line 1294; the session estimate is instead derived from each component's plan metadata (`.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1-1294,623,723-727`; `tools/plan.py:21-58`).
- The catalog handler uses imperative path matching for `GET /health` and `GET /price/<sku>`; do not assume that a static route scan captures these endpoints (`components/catalog/service.py:24-34`).
- The generated fanout instructions reference a `component-analysis` skill path that is not present in the repository; verify it before relying on fanout instructions (`tools/fanout.sh:13-15`).
- The queue `session` docstring omits `start-error`, and the module docstring describes fewer default agent logins than the code configures (`.github/bible/bible_queue.py:36,60,413-429`).
- Mermaid diagrams were checked by reading their syntax, not rendered; diagram and graph readers should validate presentation in their own renderer (`README.md`; `hld/01-system-context.md`).

## Open questions

The resolved answers establish that both catalog access modes are intentional and the fanout skill path is a stale leftover that must remain unchanged (`components/orders/orders.py:5,19-20,35-42`; `components/orders/catalog_client.py:1-4,19-23`; `tools/fanout.sh:13-15`).

## Responsibility

This component coordinates the Mode B analysis workflow through a `start`, `reconcile`, or `delta` CLI command. `Queue` reads tracker and session state from GitHub, assigns work, handles retries and human holds, checks component completion, and opens review pull requests; `GitHub` wraps the REST and GraphQL operations. (`.github/bible/bible_queue.py:9-11,473-1241`)

The `bible-plan.yml` workflow starts a run from a manual dispatch, `bible-queue.yml` invokes reconciliation on demand or every 15 minutes, and `bible-delta.yml` writes changed paths to a file and starts delta processing after a default-branch push. (`.github/workflows/bible-plan.yml:7-8`, `.github/workflows/bible-plan.yml:50-54`, `.github/workflows/bible-queue.yml:7-10`, `.github/workflows/bible-queue.yml:34-37`, `.github/workflows/bible-delta.yml:6-10`, `.github/workflows/bible-delta.yml:31-38`)

`poc-assign-copilot.yml` independently creates an issue and assigns Copilot through its inline `gh api` command; it does not invoke the queue or check out repository code. Its required `task` input defaults to an instruction to create `docs/poc-hello.md` with one line, and the input becomes the issue body passed to Copilot. (`.github/workflows/poc-assign-copilot.yml:18-21,31-37,55-69`)

No other analysis component calls into this component or is called by it (inferred: repository search for `bible_queue|\.github/bible/` in `*.py` and `*.yml` returned seven references, including the toolkit's mirrored revision rule). The queue's `delta` method does call the analysis toolkit's `components` helpers, which are outside the component catalog. (`.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1181-1241`)

## Errors and resilience

`GitHub.call` returns `None` for an allowed 404, turns other HTTP errors and URL/timeout/OS errors into `RuntimeError`, and decodes empty responses as `{}`. `main` converts `RuntimeError` to `SystemExit`; `Queue.reconcile` catches exceptions per tracker, while `Queue.run` catches component errors individually and continues other selected components. (`.github/bible/bible_queue.py:121-133,577-642,1262-1294`)

Session failures retry once and then create a human hold; successful sessions are gated by allowed-file paths and state/fingerprint checks before their PR is merged or exposed for review. (`.github/bible/bible_queue.py:555-575,794-852,681-793`)

## Logging and monitoring

The queue logs missing/invalid tracker settings, per-tracker exceptions, component gate output, tracker state rows, and delta issue creation or duplicate detection. (`.github/bible/bible_queue.py:577-642,853-879,1181-1241`)

## Summary

`main` exposes the `start`, `reconcile`, and `delta` CLI commands. It constructs `Queue` and `GitHub`; `Queue` coordinates tracker/session state and delegates repository operations to `GitHub`, whose methods build REST requests and a GraphQL ready-for-review mutation. `Queue.delta` also imports component-membership helpers from the analysis toolkit. The module guard invokes `main` when the file runs as a script. ## Module-level code

The module imports Python standard-library utilities and initializes queue labels, environment-derived agent settings, regexes, and timing/verification constants. (`.github/bible/bible_queue.py:42-98`)

It declares the `GitHub` API client (`.github/bible/bible_queue.py:104-347`) and helper functions (`.github/bible/bible_queue.py:352-468`). It declares the `Queue` coordinator (`.github/bible/bible_queue.py:473-1241`). The CLI `main` parses arguments, and the module guard calls it when executed as a script (`.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1244-1294`).

## Surprises

`tarball` limits download size and archive member count/unpacked bytes, skips non-file/non-directory members, and checks normalized targets against the destination root before writing them. (`.github/bible/bible_queue.py:267-303`)

The `Queue.session` docstring lists four result states, but the code also returns `start-error` when `GitHub.start_error` is truthy. (`.github/bible/bible_queue.py:490-495`)

`Queue.component` builds `closed_revise` after a human hold but does not use it later in the method; it separately builds and uses `all_revise`. (`.github/bible/bible_queue.py:637-641`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:755-761`)

## Responsibility

The component stores three product records in the module-level `_PRODUCTS` dictionary and provides price and stock lookups (`components/catalog/catalog.py:8-12,15-29`). `orders` imports this module and calls `price_of` and `in_stock` directly (`components/orders/orders.py:5,19-20,35-42`). The HTTP server also offers GET handling for health and price paths, with `price_of` supplying the price response (`components/catalog/service.py:24-34`). Catalog code includes functions to fetch and apply supplier data, but no feed scheduling or orchestration is defined in this component (`components/catalog/catalog.py:36-47`).

**Output and side effects**: returns a `ThreadingHTTPServer` bound to `(host, port)` with `CatalogHandler` as its request handler (`components/catalog/service.py:40-43`).

## Module-level code

The file imports `json`, `os`, `urllib.parse`, HTTP server classes, and the sibling catalog module, then defines the handler and server factory (`components/catalog/service.py:7-43`). Only when run as `__main__`, it creates the server, prints its address, and calls `serve_forever()` (`components/catalog/service.py:46-49`).

## Surprises

The path for routing comes from `urlsplit(self.path).path`, so the query portion does not participate in the route match (`components/catalog/service.py:25-28`).

## Responsibility

The component provides order line and discounted-total calculations, validates requested quantities against catalog stock, and submits order settlements (`components/orders/orders.py:19-51`). Its `catalog_client` module also resolves a catalog service URL and requests prices over HTTP (`components/orders/catalog_client.py:14-29`). Per the [recorded answer to Q1](../../ledger/components/orders/questions.md), `orders.py`'s direct import is used when catalog and orders run in one process (today's deployment), while `catalog_client.py` is intended for orders running as a separate service; the code confirms the direct import and HTTP client behavior (`components/orders/orders.py:5,19-20,35-41`; `components/orders/catalog_client.py:1-4,14-23`). The answer also notes that tests are the HTTP path's in-repository callers; the client uses plain HTTP to `CATALOG_URL`, defaulting to `http://127.0.0.1:8001` (`components/orders/catalog_client.py:11,14-23`; `components/orders/test_catalog_client.py:37-62`). The test modules invoke `unittest.main()` when run as scripts (`components/orders/test_orders.py:11-12`, `components/orders/test_catalog_client.py:65-66`).

**Steps**

1. Sums `line_total(sku, qty)` for every pair in `lines` to get `subtotal`, then sums each quantity to get `items` (`components/orders/orders.py:25-26`).

```text
items = sum(qty for each line)
discount = LOYALTY_DISCOUNT if loyal else 0
if items >= BULK_THRESHOLD: discount = max(discount, BULK_DISCOUNT)
return round(subtotal * (1 - discount), 2)
```

### Reader test

1. The repository combines a sample catalog/orders app with GitHub Actions automation for analysis sessions; its intended business customer is not declared. See `README.md`, “In two minutes,” and `hld/01-system-context.md`, “Purpose and scope.”
2. The catalog is a Python module with an optional HTTP server, orders is a Python library, and the queue/tooling run as Python and GitHub Actions/Bash. See `hld/02-architecture.md`, “Component architecture,” and the component READMEs.
3. Catalog can start with `python3 -m components.catalog.service` on its configurable bind/port; queue and planning jobs run on hosted Ubuntu Actions runners, while deployment topology for catalog/orders is unspecified. See `hld/02-architecture.md`, “Deployment architecture.”
4. Catalog accepts GET paths `/health` and `/price/<sku>`; the handler contains no authentication or authorization check. Queue entry points are workflow dispatches and scheduled/push events. See `lld/api/catalog/catalog.md`, both endpoint cards, and `hld/02-architecture.md`.
5. Outbound calls include supplier and payment HTTP, optional catalog-client HTTP, and GitHub REST/GraphQL/CLI calls; endpoints and schemes are listed by caller. See `hld/03-integrations.md`, “Outbound calls,” and `reference/configuration.md`.
6. Product records are in process-local `_PRODUCTS`; queue state is held in GitHub issues/labels/PRs; gate work uses a temporary filesystem workspace. See `lld/data-dictionary.md`, “Stores,” “GitHub-backed workflow records,” and “Files read and written.”
7. Twenty rules are enumerated with enforcement locations across catalog, orders, queue, and component-tool passes. See the “Business rules” sections of the four component READMEs and `knowledge/AGENT-CONTEXT.md`, “Rules the code enforces.”
8. Environment variables, workflow inputs, and source constants configure the components; the `BIBLE_ASSIGN_TOKEN` repository secret is mapped to `GH_TOKEN`, with no value documented. See `reference/configuration.md` and `hld/06-cross-cutting.md`, “Secrets.”
9. Requests use explicit timeouts, but ordinary network calls have no retry; GitHub failures can stop queue operations, and only failed agent sessions receive the queue's one retry. See `hld/03-integrations.md`, “Timeouts and failures,” and `hld/06-cross-cutting.md`, “Errors and resilience.”
10. The catalog exposes `/health`; the queue prints messages and workflow results, but no metrics or tracing are implemented. See `lld/api/catalog/catalog.md`, “GET /health,” and `hld/06-cross-cutting.md`, “Observability.”
11. There is no application build or production deployment declared; existing tests use `unittest`, and the tool gate runs discovery during pass 3. Several order methods are not covered by tests. See `hld/02-architecture.md`, “Build and deployment,” and `hld/06-cross-cutting.md`, “Testing.”
12. `CatalogHandler.do_GET` returns 200 for `/health`, returns a looked-up price for a known `/price/` path followed by an SKU, and returns 404 for an unknown SKU or unmatched path. See `lld/api/catalog/catalog.md`, “GET /health” and the price endpoint card.
13. `_PRODUCTS` is initialized from three records; `apply_feed` changes only each known SKU's `price` and `stock`, while lookup helpers read those values. See `lld/data-dictionary.md`, “Catalog products,” and `lld/catalog/catalog.md`, “Data.”
14. `fetch_supplier_feed` is the supplier HTTP caller; its network errors propagate and no automatic invocation is shown. See `hld/03-integrations.md`, “Outbound calls,” and `lld/catalog/catalog.md`, `fetch_supplier_feed`.
15. The direct catalog import is the current orders path, while the HTTP client is for separate-service mode and has tests as its only callers; the feed's “nightly” docstring has no matching scheduler. See `lld/orders/README.md`, “Outbound calls,” and `reference/risks-and-surprises.md`.

The front page and the coverage ledger say the coverage gate passes. When I ran it, it returned GAPS. heading_path: Data dictionary and mind map findings
text:
## Data dictionary and mind map findings

- Mind map: every leaf names a page that exists; all four components are on it.
- Data dictionary: I did not open the schema-level check for every store. Its `components.json` and `status.json` citations are off (V-007).

## Knowledge base findings

- `graph.json` carries `generated: 2026-11-23T22:52:29`. The checkout gives every file the same time, so I cannot say it is newer than the pages. Because the pages' line numbers are stale (V-001), regenerate it after the revision.
- I did not take the ten `analysis` and five `name-unique` edges, so the share of wrong edges is unknown.
- `AGENT-CONTEXT.md` states the three required limits (dynamic dispatch, `name-unique` and `analysis` leads, snapshot date). Seventeen of its citations point at `bible_queue.py`; the sampled ones are off (row 260 held, 280 held).

## Readability and prose findings

I read the front page, one HLD page and the `catalog` card pages: they open with a summary, are plain and in a sensible order. No numbered claim references or template text found. The only readability issue is V-008. I checked only a few sentences of the HLD pages against their citations: no sentence went beyond its citation.

## Ledger findings

- Completeness: all seven folders and 20 files in scope are in `ledger/coverage-ledger.md`.
- "Read in full": every file is listed as read in full; for `bible_queue.py` the ledger is not true of the current file (V-001, V-005).
- No "not read", "sampled" or "excluded" rows exist.

## Consistency findings

- V-004 (gate result stated as PASS), V-008.
- The README, `status.json` and the component reports all place `tools`, `catalog`, `orders` and `bible-mode-b` consistently; names agree across the mind map, HLD and LLD pages I opened.
- No secret value found in the pages I read; the token is named only as `secrets.BIBLE_ASSIGN_TOKEN`.

## Limits

- A reduced sample was checked, not every citation, and groups A and C were only partly covered; rows 620 to 1040 and 1660 to 1740 were not judged.
- The coverage script matches names; it does not read meaning. The depth audit covers seven cards.
- Verification shows the analysis matches the code, not that the code matches what runs in production.
- Diagrams were read, not rendered. The knowledge-graph edge checks were not done, so the graph is a lead only.
- If the same model wrote and verified the analysis (the author's model is not recorded), a person or another model should re-check V-001 to V-005 and a few confirmed statements.
